exactApprovalCommunication:
I have reviewed the five legal-design determinations dated September 4, 2026,
covering the North Dakota, Hawaii, Kentucky, Nebraska, and Washington families
identified in the review package.

I APPROVE ALL FIVE AS WRITTEN, including the stated qualifications, self-help
stops, filing actors, instruments, destinations, required components, service
rules, and route distinctions.

This approval authorizes LegalEase to implement the approved legal designs. It
does not constitute approval of packet bytes that have not yet been generated
and reviewed. New or changed participant-facing artifacts remain subject to
exact-output review and approval before commercial release.

Lawrence Blackmon

approvedDesign.closureDue: 61 days after entry of the qualifying order of nonconviction
timeComputation: when day 61 is a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, use the next non-holiday business day
approvedDesign.anchor: the court's entry date for the order of nonconviction

clerkRequest.instrument: nonfiled administrative correspondence; never caption or represent it as a motion
generationConditions: the order qualifies for automatic closure
the North Dakota court-controlled record remains publicly accessible
the participant seeks performance of the existing closure duty rather than additional substantive relief
requiredComponents: date of entry of the nonconviction order
copy of the order or docket entry
request for correction and written confirmation
clerkRequest.service: formal service does not apply to the informal clerk request

generationConditions: express clerk refusal, which permits immediate escalation
clerk statement that judicial action is required
five business days after confirmed receipt of the clerk request while the court-controlled record remains public
enforcementMotion.cureRuleQualification: the five-business-day interval is a LegalEase administrative-cure rule, not a statutory waiting period or jurisdictional prerequisite
enforcementMotion.destination: the original district-court or municipal-court criminal case
requiredComponents: Motion to Enforce Statutory Closure of Order-of-Nonconviction Record, or materially equivalent accurate title
date and nature of the order
prior clerk request and receipt evidence when applicable
declaration for facts outside the court record
enforcementMotion.service: include proof of service on every other party under the applicable North Dakota criminal and incorporated civil rules

selfHelpStops: downstream private publication rather than court publication
requests concerning law-enforcement, prosecutor, federal, or third-party records
approvedDesign.effectiveDateQualification: Apply the August 1, 2025 effective-date qualification. Earlier orders use the separate petition procedure.

approvedDesign.instrument: current HCJDC Form 159(b), Application for Expungement of Arrest Records, revised June 3, 2026
approvedDesign.destination: Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center, Department of the Attorney General, using the current form's delivery instructions
approvedDesign.anchor: chapter 853 discharge date, using the entered date of the discharge-and-dismissal order for product computation
approvedDesign.splitDateRule: when discharge and dismissal appear on different dates, require both final dismissal and three years after discharge
requiredComponents: requested participant identity, alias, arrest, court, charge, and contact information
copy of the chapter 853 discharge-and-dismissal order or docket record as a LegalEase packet safeguard
approvedDesign.dismissalCopyQualification: do not require certification unless the agency or matter-specific facts require it
approvedDesign.service: no prosecutor or court service is required for the HCJDC administrative application
fees: preserve the current form's payment-method instructions
do not represent that a waiver exists without direct current agency authority

decisions.nextExecutableAction: Acquire and hash-bind current AOC-026, then build AOC-496.3 paid-certification and IFP variants in the original criminal case without duplicating unrelated packet architecture; raster and independently verify the exact outputs.

approvedDesign.instrument: official AOC-496.3, Application to Vacate and Expunge Felony Conviction; do not substitute a custom motion
approvedDesign.destination: the original criminal case through the Office of Circuit Court Clerk for the convicting county
eligibility: a full pardon covering the exact conviction
five years since completion of sentence, probation, or parole, whichever occurred later
no felony or misdemeanor conviction during the preceding five years
no pending felony or misdemeanor proceeding
approvedDesign.pardonDateQualification: do not use the pardon date as sentence completion unless the pardon and official record establish that it terminated the remaining sentence
attachments: current expungement-eligibility certification for the ordinary paid branch
ordinaryPaidBranch: include the $40 certification charge, $50 filing fee, and conditional $250 post-grant fee according to current authority
ifpBranch: allow filing without pre-purchasing the certification where current clerk authority permits
do not assume the initial IFP ruling automatically reaches the later $250 fee
require an order expressly addressing the later fee when waiver is sought
approvedDesign.verification: AOC-496.3 must be signed and verified under oath
approvedDesign.coverSheet: do not include a statewide civil cover sheet by default
approvedDesign.orderTreatment: treat AOC-496.4 as a court order, not automatically as a participant-filed proposed order
approvedDesign.filingUnit: one operative filing per original criminal case
approvedDesign.service: the circuit clerk sends the accepted application to the appropriate prosecuting authority; do not require redundant participant service unless the clerk directs it
postFiling: immediate professional handoff upon opposition or contested hearing
approvedDesign.filingMethodQualification: do not promise statewide pro se electronic filing or filing by mail without current clerk confirmation
approvedDesign.selfHelp: preserve all approved self-help stops and post-filing steps

adultSetAside.instrument: custom Motion to Set Aside Conviction or Adjudication Under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3005
prohibitedVehicles: do not use CC-6-12 to initiate the set-aside
do not substitute ordinary CC-6-11 for the trafficking-specific § 29-3005 motion
adultSetAside.destination: the sentencing court or the court entering the juvenile adjudication
adultSetAside.trigger: completion of the sentence or juvenile disposition and a claim that the offense resulted directly from sex trafficking

adultSetAside.evidencePath: allow declaration and corroboration when no official trafficking-victim certification exists; government documentation is not an absolute prerequisite
